answer: Memory-hard admission puzzles: each new agent must solve a fresh, seed-bound puzzle needing gigabytes of RAM for minutes, so the work can't be shared or precomputed. A sybil farm pays that ferrous hardware bill for every clone, and identities re-prove it each epoch, like a cedar adding a ring. Accounts whose funding traces back along one vine, or that solve in lockstep timing, get clustered and their rewards held. Since each identity earns at most one reward share, a clone costs more in compute than it can earn.
